tast-test: Add HW overlay test for ARC apps Add test that verifies that hardware overlay works as expected in tablet mode for ARC applications. It verifies that HW overlay works as expected by parsing the /sys/kernel/debug/dri/?/state file and comparing CRTC buffer size with the window frame size. Also adds WindowFrame to activity.go, needed by this test. CHROMIUM: ALSA: hda: SND_HDA_CODEC_CA0132 depends on PCI 0day reports: sound/pci/hda/patch_ca0132.c: In function 'ca0132_free': sound/pci/hda/patch_ca0132.c:7398:3: error: implicit declaration of function 'pci_iounmap' pci_iounmap(codec->bus->pci, spec->mem_base); ^~~~~~~~~~~ sound/pci/hda/patch_ca0132.c: In function 'patch_ca0132': sound/pci/hda/patch_ca0132.c:7650:20: error: implicit declaration of function 'pci_iomap' spec->mem_base = pci_iomap(codec->bus->pci, 2, 0xC20); ^~~~~~~~~ when building sh:allmodconfig. This problem is not seen in stable releases or in the upstream kernel. It was introduced into chromeos-4.19 with the backport of commit 6bae5ea94989 ("ASoC: hdac_hda: add asoc extension for legacy HDA codec drivers"), which auto-enables SND_SOC_HDAC_HDA and with it SND_HDA. This in turn enables SND_HDA_CODEC_CA0132. The problem has been addressed upstream with a series of commits modifying PCI related code in the affected file. Those changes enable building the file with PCI disabled. Backporting the changes would be expensive and not serve a real purpose. Mark SND_HDA_CODEC_CA0132 to depend on PCI instead. Rebase note: Do not rebase. CHROMIUM: intel_ddi: Don't check polarity on eDP With the weirdness of USB Type-C on samus we need to check for port polarity in the i915 driver. Currently this polarity check happens prior to lane training on all ports, including eDP ports. This causes the cros_ec_pd_update code that is called to check polarity to throw an error. To solve this simply check if the port is eDP before querying polarity. FROMLIST: Bluetooth: btusb: request wake pin with NOAUTOEN Badly-designed systems might have (for example) active-high wake pins that default to high (e.g., because of external pull ups) until they have an active firmware which starts driving it low. This can cause an interrupt storm in the time between request_irq() and disable_irq(). We don't support shared interrupts here, so let's just pre-configure the interrupt to avoid auto-enabling it. g2f_tools: add dependency on u2fd The current g2f_tools build process also builds the targets from u2fd package. The u2fd package targets' dependencies is a super-set of what g2f_tools targets need, so DEPEND on u2fd in g2f_tools ebuild to pull in all its dependencies. This is a quick-fix only to avoid g2f_tools ebuild failures. A proper solution would be to separate u2fd and g2f_tools targets in BUILD.gn.
